transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been having mornings where I think it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. That scared me enough to come in. I don’t have any plan to hurt myself, but those thoughts keep coming up.
How long have you been feeling this way—days, weeks, or longer?
About a month now. It started after my sister died unexpectedly.

Since your sister passed away, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, nearly every day, or does your mood tend to lift at times when you're distracted or with others?

I still go to book club and the dance night, but I don’t really enjoy them the way I used to. It’s like I’m there behind a pane of glass. Even gardening or cooking for the neighbors doesn’t give me that little lift anymore.
Before this past month, have you ever had a period of at least two weeks in your life where you felt persistently sad, lost interest in things, or had similar symptoms like this?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another time that felt quite like this.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty about things unrelated to your sister's death, nearly every day?

I keep replaying those last weeks with my sister. I think I should have called more, listened better, done something—anything—more helpful, even though I know I probably couldn’t have changed what happened.
Have you noticed changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up much earlier than usual—nearly every night over this past month?
I do. I fall asleep in bits and pieces, and then I’m awake before dawn with my mind already turning. Most mornings I can’t really settle back down before the day starts.
Over this past month, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy nearly every day, even after resting?
Yes. Even simple errands, or getting papers together for the Cultural Center, leave me worn out. It feels like I’m moving through thick mud.
Over this past month, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight, either increased or decreased, without trying?
Food just doesn’t appeal to me much lately. I’ll make some toast or soup, and then by evening realize I’ve barely eaten. I’m not trying to lose weight.

Over this past month, how much have these symptoms affected your ability to keep up with your usual daily responsibilities—work, chores, or social commitments—are you still managing them, even with difficulty, or have you found yourself unable to carry them out at all?

I’m still managing some things, but not the way I usually do. I had to ask another volunteer to cover parts of the Juneteenth budgeting workshop because I just can’t keep up with the preparation. And I’ve been turning down neighbors and friends more than I normally would.
You mentioned thoughts that it might be easier not to wake up—how often are these thoughts occurring, and do they ever feel hard to push away or resist?

They’ve been coming up in the mornings fairly often. I’ll wake up and think it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up at all. That’s what scared me enough to ask for help. But I don’t have a plan to hurt myself.
